questions.q: What is a 'mass addition' in Oracle Fusion Fixed Assets?
options: A candidate fixed asset staged for review, waiting to be formally created
A finalized, depreciating asset already on the books
A journal entry posted to the general ledger
A rejected row with no further action possible
questions.explain: A mass addition is staged, candidate data — not yet a real, depreciating asset — waiting for the Mass Additions Create and posting steps.

questions.q: Besides the Mass Additions Create FBDI template, what is the other common source of mass additions?
options: Manual entry only, with no other source possible
General Ledger journal entries
A capital-coded Payables invoice line, which automatically generates a mass addition
AutoInvoice transactions
questions.explain: When a Payables invoice line is coded as a capital asset purchase rather than an ordinary expense, it automatically generates a candidate mass addition.

questions.q: Which interface table holds staged fixed asset mass additions?
options: GL_INTERFACE
FA_MASS_ADDITIONS
RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL
AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE
questions.explain: FA_MASS_ADDITIONS is the Fixed Assets staging table where candidate asset rows land, regardless of which of the two sources they came from.

questions.q: What two distinct actions does a staged mass addition typically go through before it becomes a real, depreciating asset?
options: Only uploading to UCM — nothing else is required
Running AutoInvoice twice
Deleting and re-creating the row twice
Mass Additions Create, followed by a separate posting step
questions.explain: Fixed Assets additions go through a create step that turns staged data into a formal, reviewable record, and then a separate posting step that adds it to the books and starts depreciation.

questions.q: Why does Fixed Assets include an extra review step that journals and invoices don't emphasize as heavily?
options: Because details like asset category, useful life, and depreciation method benefit from human review before being locked in, especially for additions that arrived automatically from Payables
Because Fixed Assets data never needs validation
Because the FBDI pipeline doesn't apply to Fixed Assets at all
Because posting is purely optional and rarely performed
questions.explain: The extra create-then-post pattern gives a person a chance to confirm category, useful life, and depreciation method before an asset is finalized and starts depreciating.
